### **9.5 UC-47: Perform Clinical Examination** {#9.5-uc-47:-perform-clinical-examination}

| Primary Actors | Doctor | Secondary Actors | None |
| ----: | :---- | ----: | :---- |
| **Description** | The Doctor examines a patient called in through UC-44 on the “Khám lâm sàng” tab, following outpatient Form 15/BV1. The Doctor records: the reason for visit; the vital signs; the general and body-part findings; the preliminary diagnosis, as one or more ICD-10 codes. From this screen the Doctor goes on to paraclinical orders (UC-49) or to the conclusion (UC-56). |  |  |
| **Preconditions** | The Doctor is signed in (UC-01) with an active account and is not required to change the password. The Doctor is assigned to an active examination room and is on duty there now (BR-05, BR-19, BR-55). The visit belongs to that room, is assigned to this Doctor, is “Đang khám” and is not skipped. Its medical record is Open (BR-32). |  |  |
| **Normal Flow** | The Doctor opens the visit from UC-44, or clicks its row in UC-43. The system checks the Doctor, room, shift and visit. On the first opening it creates the outpatient medical record and the examination sheet, and records the view in the audit log (BR-42). The system shows: the patient and visit details; the drug allergies; the previous visits; the medical history (UC-39); the saved examination data. The Doctor enters or updates: 4.1. “Lý do khám / triệu chứng chính”: prefilled from reception, 2–1,000 characters (BR-95). 4.2. “Sinh hiệu”: at least one value, within the ranges of BR-98. BMI is calculated from weight and height. 4.3. “1. Toàn thân”: at most 4,000 characters. “2. Khám bộ phận”: at most 2,000 characters (BR-99). 4.4. “Chẩn đoán ban đầu (ICD-10)”: one or more codes. Each code must be valid on the visit day, be the most detailed code and fit the patient’s sex (BR-31, BR-46, BR-51, BR-100). The code and name are saved as a snapshot. The Doctor clicks “Lưu”. The system checks the reason for visit and the vital signs, then saves in one transaction (BR-119): the examination data; the vital signs, with the Doctor as measurer; an audit row with the old and new values (BR-42). The system shows MSG03 (“Hồ sơ khám lâm sàng cập nhật thành công.”). The visit stays “Đang khám”. To continue, the Doctor opens the “Chỉ định cận lâm sàng” tab (UC-49) or the “Kết luận” tab (UC-56). The system saves first as in step 5, and also requires at least one preliminary-diagnosis code. |  |  |
| **Alternative Flows** | AF-01 (at step 3): Update medical history or allergies1.1. The Doctor adds or edits an item in UC-39 (BR-23, BR-93). The panel refreshes. AF-02 (at step 3): Transfer the patient2.1. Before the first save, the “Chuyển phòng” tab is available (UC-48). AF-03 (at step 1): Visit waiting for paraclinical services or for the conclusion3.1. The examination opens read-only, and it cannot be saved. AF-04: Leave with unsaved changes4.1. The system shows MSG38 with “Tiếp tục chỉnh sửa” and “Loại bỏ”. Data already saved is kept. |  |  |
| **Exception Flows** | EF-01 (at step 5 or 7): Invalid data1.1. The message is shown under the field, and nothing is saved: missing field or no vital sign: MSG02; too long: MSG08; vital sign out of range, or diastolic not below systolic: MSG05. EF-02 (at step 7): No preliminary diagnosis2.1. MSG02 under “Chẩn đoán ban đầu”. The tab does not open. EF-03 (at step 4.4): Invalid ICD-10 code3.1. The code is no longer valid, is not the most detailed, or does not fit the patient’s sex: MSG40. EF-04 (at step 2 or 5): Not allowed4.1. Not an active Doctor, or not the Doctor of the visit: MSG13. Off duty: MSG48. No room: MSG99. Record closed: MSG68. Visit not found: MSG39. EF-05 (at step 5): Changed by another request5.1. MSG75; the Doctor reloads. EF-06: Session expired or system error6.1. Session expired: MSG12, and the system returns to UC-01. Server unreachable: MSG96. Other errors: MSG80. Nothing is shown as saved before the server confirms it. |  |  |
| **Postconditions** | Success: the examination data, the vital signs and the preliminary diagnosis are saved in the open medical record, and the change is in the audit log. The visit stays “Đang khám” until UC-49 or UC-56. Failure: nothing is saved. |  |  |
| **Business Rules** | BR-02, BR-05, BR-19, BR-23, BR-31, BR-32, BR-42, BR-46, BR-51, BR-55, BR-93, BR-95, BR-98, BR-99, BR-100, BR-119  |  |  |
| **Messages** | BR-02, BR-05, BR-19, BR-23, BR-31, BR-32, BR-42, BR-46, BR-51, BR-55, BR-93, BR-95, BR-98, BR-99, BR-100, BR-119  |  |  |

### **9.6 UC-48: Transfer Patient to Another Room** {#9.6-uc-48:-transfer-patient-to-another-room}

| Primary Actors | Doctor | Secondary Actors | None |
| ----: | :---- | ----: | :---- |
| **Description** | During a valid shift, the Doctor may transfer a patient of their room who is waiting for examination or has been called but whose current-visit medical record has not yet been opened. The destination must be a different active examination room with a Doctor scheduled that day. A transfer reason is mandatory. The system retains the same visit, issues the next queue number for the destination room, marks "Transferred from room ...", and places the patient after priority patients but before ordinary patients. After a successful transfer, the new queue number is shown and the examination ticket may be reprinted; no additional examination fee is charged (BR-18, BR-24, BR-96, BR-97). |  |  |
| **Preconditions** | The Doctor is signed in (UC-01), assigned to an examination room, and working a valid shift (BR-05, BR-19, BR-55). The patient belongs to the Doctor's room and is waiting for examination, or was called but the current-visit medical record has not been opened. The visit has not been completed or abandoned. Note: The existence of an eligible destination room is checked in the Normal/Alternative Flow, not assumed as a precondition (AF-03, BR-96). |  |  |
| **Normal Flow** | The Doctor opens the examination-waiting list (UC-43) or a called patient's details before opening the medical record (UC-44). The Doctor selects an eligible patient and clicks "Transfer Room". The system checks the latest visit status, source room, shift, and whether the medical record has already been opened (MSG56 if opened; MSG99 if status changed). The "Transfer Examination Room" screen displays patient name/code, birth date, sex, visit type and insurance card if applicable, visit date/code, current room, current queue number, reason for visit, and visit status. The transfer form provides required "Destination Room" and "Transfer Reason" fields, optional "Notes", and "Cancel"/"Confirm Transfer" buttons. The system retrieves eligible rooms under BR-07/BR-96: different from the source, active, with a Doctor scheduled that day, and otherwise eligible to accept the patient. The system lists eligible rooms with code, name, department, location, and scheduled Doctor information where available. The Doctor selects a destination room. The system displays its details and permits entry of the transfer reason. The Doctor enters a reason of 5–500 characters (BR-97); MSG100 applies if the length is invalid. The Doctor may add optional notes. The Doctor clicks "Confirm Transfer". The system rechecks that: (a) the patient remains assigned to the source room; (b) the visit is neither completed nor abandoned; (c) the patient is waiting or has been called without opening the record; (d) the destination differs from the source, is active, and has a Doctor scheduled that day; (e) the reason has 5–500 characters; and (f) the transferring Doctor is in a valid shift. The system atomically assigns the next non-duplicated queue number in the destination room under BR-18. The system updates the existing visit: destination room and queue number, "Waiting for Examination" status, transfer marker, source room, and transfer time. The system saves transfer history: visit code, source/destination rooms, old/new queue numbers, transfer reason, user, time, and optional notes. The system removes the patient from the source room's waiting list. The system inserts the patient in the destination room's "Waiting for Examination" list with "Transferred from room ...". S The existing visit ID and receipts/fees remain unchanged; transferring rooms creates no additional examination charge (BR-24). The system records the relevant change/audit history. The system displays MSG24 with the destination room and new queue number. The system shows updated visit details and the "Reprint Examination Ticket" action. The use case ends successfully. |  |  |
| **Alternative Flows** | AF-01 (at step 11): Doctor cancels. 1.1. Clicking "Cancel" prompts MSG38 if there are unsaved changes. On confirmed cancellation the screen closes and the room, queue number, and visit status remain unchanged. AF-02 (at step 23): Reprint ticket. 2.1. The Doctor clicks "Reprint Examination Ticket". The system prepares a ticket using the existing visit ID, new queue number, destination room, and location, then continues with UC-41. 2.2. Reprinting creates neither a new visit nor a new examination charge. AF-03 (at step 6): No eligible destination room. 3.1. If no other room meets BR-96, the system displays an explanatory notice, disables "Confirm Transfer", and keeps the patient in the source room. AF-04 (at step 3): Patient called, record not opened. 4.1. The system permits transfer under BR-24. After transfer, the visit becomes "Waiting for Examination" in the destination and no longer remains in "Calling" status in the source room. AF-05 (at step 11): No optional note. 5.1. The system accepts a blank note and continues at step 12\. |  |  |
| **Exception Flows** | EF-01 (at steps 3 or 13): Medical record already opened. 1.1. The system displays MSG56, rejects transfer, and retains the original room/queue/status. EF-02 (at steps 10 or 13): Missing transfer reason. 2.1. The system displays MSG31; the Doctor supplies the reason and returns to step 10\. EF-03 (at step 13): Transfer reason violates BR-97. 3.1. The system displays MSG100 for fewer than 5 or more than 500 characters, blocks confirmation, and returns to step 10\. EF-04 (at step 13): Destination room no longer eligible. 4.1. If the destination is inactive, lacks a Doctor scheduled that day, or fails an acceptance condition, display MSG53 and allow a different selection (return to step 8). EF-05 (at step 13): Visit is no longer transferable. 5.1. If it has already transferred, been skipped, completed, abandoned, or otherwise changed contrary to BR-24, reject transfer, show MSG99, reload details, and end. EF-06 (at steps 13–16): Concurrent transfer or queue-number conflict. 6.1. Prevent duplicate queue numbers and repeat transfers. If an atomic transaction cannot complete, roll back all partial changes; show MSG99 for a changed visit, or MSG80 for a system transaction failure. The Doctor may reload and retry if still eligible. EF-07 (at step 23): Reprint fails. 7.1. Display MSG49, retain the successful transfer, and allow a retry. EF-08 (at steps 3 or 13): Doctor outside a valid shift. 8.1. Display MSG48 and reject the transfer. EF-09 (at any step): Session expired. 9.1. Display MSG12 and redirect to UC-01. EF-10 (at steps 3–22): System/network error. 10.1. Display MSG80. If transfer was not committed, preserve the previous room and queue; never report success before confirmation. Allow refresh and retry. |  |  |
| **Postconditions** | Success: The patient belongs to an eligible destination examination room with a new queue number and "Transferred from room ..." marker, ordered under BR-18. Transfer history is saved; the visit ID and payment records are retained, no additional examination fee arises, and a reprinted ticket is available. Failure: No invalid transfer is created and an unsuccessful transaction does not alter the previously saved room, queue number, or visit status. |  |  |
| **Business Rules** | BR-02, BR-05, BR-07, BR-18, BR-19, BR-24, BR-42, BR-53, BR-55, BR-96, BR-97 |  |  |
| **Messages** | MSG08, MSG12, MSG31, MSG38, MSG48, MSG49, MSG53, MSG56, MSG80, MSG99, MSG100 |  |  |

### **9.7 UC-49: Order Paraclinical Services** {#9.7-uc-49:-order-paraclinical-services}

| Primary Actors | Doctor | Secondary Actors | Cashier (collects the paraclinical fee afterwards) |
| ----: | :---- | ----: | :---- |
| **Description** | As a Doctor, I want to select paraclinical services, review the estimated cost with the patient and confirm the order, so that a paraclinical receipt is created and, once paid, the services are routed to the paraclinical rooms (BR-25, BR-26, BR-28). Only active services can be ordered (BR-10). |  |  |
| **Preconditions** | 1\. The visit is In Examination by the Doctor and its medical record is open (UC-47), or the Doctor is reviewing results before the conclusion and the record is not closed (UC-56, more tests needed). |  |  |
| **Normal Flow** | 1\. The Doctor clicks Order Paraclinical Services. 2\. The system shows the active paraclinical services grouped by type and group (Lab, Imaging, Functional) with a search box, the clinic price and insurance price of each service (BR-08, BR-10). 3\. The Doctor selects one or more services and may add a clinical note for the technician. 4\. The system shows the estimated cost per service and in total, split into the insurance amount and the patient amount according to the visit type and coverage rate (BR-27). 5\. The Doctor explains the services and the estimated cost to the patient (BR-25). 6\. The patient agrees; the Doctor clicks Confirm Order. 7\. The system checks that at least one service is selected, that every service is Active and that no service appears twice in the order. 8\. The system creates one paraclinical order per selected service (status Pending Payment) with the current prices stored (BR-09), and one paraclinical receipt (status Pending) with one line per service (BR-26, BR-27). 9\. The system sets the visit to Waiting for Paraclinical, records the order in the audit log and shows MSG63. 10\. The Doctor prints the paraclinical order slip (UC-50) and tells the patient to pay at the cashier counter. The receipt appears in the Cashier's waiting payment list (UC-69). |  |  |
| **Alternative Flows** | **AF-01 (at step 8): The patient amount of the receipt is 0** 1\. The system sets the receipt to Paid automatically and releases the orders immediately: each order becomes Waiting and is routed to the Active room with the fewest waiting patients among the rooms that perform the service (BR-26, BR-28). 2\. The order slip shows the assigned rooms. *\=\>Continue at step 9\.* **AF-02 (at step 6): The patient does not agree before the order is confirmed** 1\. The Doctor does not confirm; no order or receipt is created. The Doctor records the refusal in the findings (UC-47, AF-03). *\=\>The use case ends.* **AF-03 (at step 3): An insured patient selects a service outside insurance coverage** 1\. The system marks the service "Not covered"; it is charged at the clinic price and the patient still pays it (BR-26, BR-27). *\=\>Continue at step 4\.* **AF-04 (at step 1): Additional tests after reviewing results (from UC-56)** 1\. The visit goes back from Waiting for Conclusion to Waiting for Paraclinical when the new order is confirmed; a new receipt is created for the new services. *\=\>Continue at step 2\.* |  |  |
| **Exception Flows** | **EF-01 (at step 7): No service selected or duplicate service** 1\. The system shows MSG02 or MSG07. *\=\>Return to step 3\.* **EF-02 (at step 7): A selected service was deactivated meanwhile** 1\. The system shows MSG42 and removes the service from the selection. *\=\>Return to step 3\.* **EF-03 (at step 8): Session expired or system error** 1\. The system shows MSG12 or MSG99; no order or receipt is created (all or nothing). *\=\>Return to step 6\.* |  |  |
| **Postconditions** | Success: the orders and the paraclinical receipt exist. The orders reach the paraclinical rooms only after the receipt is Paid (UC-71) or immediately if the patient amount is 0 (BR-26). A confirmed order cannot be cancelled by the Doctor; if the receipt is still unpaid at the end of the day, it becomes Cancelled together with its orders and the visit becomes Abandoned (BR-22, BR-25). Failure / Cancelled: no order and no receipt are created. |  |  |
| **Business Rules** | BR-08, BR-09, BR-10, BR-19, BR-22, BR-25, BR-26, BR-27, BR-28; Data rules: Paraclinical order content, Price snapshot (I.3.3) |  |  |
| **Messages** | MSG02, MSG07, MSG12, MSG42, MSG63, MSG99 |  |  |

### **9.8 UC-50: Print Paraclinical Order** {#9.8-uc-50:-print-paraclinical-order}

| Primary Actors | Doctor | Secondary Actors | None |
| ----: | :---- | ----: | :---- |
| **Description** | As a Doctor, after confirming a paraclinical order (UC-49), I want to print the order slip so that the patient knows which paraclinical rooms to go to. One sheet is printed per performing room, listing its services, room and location, following the request part of the TT 32/2023/TT-BYT forms 08/BV2 to 26/BV2.  |  |  |
| **Preconditions** | The Doctor is signed in (UC-01) with an active account and is not required to change the password.  The order exists, is not cancelled, and belongs to a visit of the Doctor (the Doctor who created the order or the Doctor assigned to the visit).  |  |  |
| **Normal Flow** | The Doctor clicks “In phiếu chỉ định” on an order, either right after confirming it in UC-49 or from the order list of the visit. The system checks the Doctor and the order (EF-01 to EF-03). The system builds the sheets:3.1. Cancelled and abandoned services are left out.3.2. Services are grouped into one sheet per performing room, sorted by room code; services keep their order-line order.3.3. Every sheet shows the order number and “Tờ {i}/{n}”. Each sheet shows:4.1. Header: facility name, address and phone (UC-77); title “PHIẾU CHỈ ĐỊNH CẬN LÂM SÀNG”; “Số: {số phiếu}”; “Tờ {i}/{n}”.4.2. Patient: full name, year of birth and age, sex, address, patient code, visit code; visit type, plus the insurance card number for an insurance visit.4.3. Ordering place: department and room of the visit.4.4. Clinical: initial diagnosis; priority “Thường” or “Cấp cứu”.4.5. Services: No., order line code, service name, quantity.4.6. “Nơi thực hiện: {tên phòng} – {vị trí}”.4.7. Footer: order time (dd/MM/yyyy HH:mm); “Bác sĩ chỉ định” with a hand-signature space and the Doctor’s name.4.8. Queue numbers and amounts are not printed. Queue numbers are assigned at release (UC-71); amounts are on the receipt (UC-72). The system records the print in the audit log (order number, number of sheets, reprint or not). The system shows the sheets and opens the browser print dialog. End: The use case ends when the Doctor closes the print dialog. |  |  |
| **Alternative Flows** | AF-01 (at step 3): Reprint1.1. If the order was printed before, the sheets show “Bản in lại” and reflect the current order, without services cancelled since.1.2. Reprinting is allowed as long as the order is not cancelled. AF-02 (at step 3): A service has no performing room2.1. This applies only to orders created before the Doctor chose rooms in UC-49 and not yet released.2.2. The sheet shows the service group name and “Phòng sẽ được chỉ định sau khi thanh toán”; these sheets come after the room sheets. |  |  |
| **Exception Flows** | EF-01 (at step 2): Not allowed1.1. The user is not an active Doctor, must change the password, or the order is not of the Doctor’s visit.1.2. The system returns FORBIDDEN and shows MSG13; nothing is recorded. EF-02 (at step 2): Order not found2.1. The system shows MSG39 (“Không tìm thấy phiếu chỉ định.”). EF-03 (at step 3): Nothing to print3.1. The order is cancelled, or all its services are cancelled.3.2. The system shows MSG104: “Phiếu chỉ định đã bị hủy hoặc không còn dịch vụ nào nên không thể in.” EF-04 (at step 4): Facility information missing4.1. The system shows “Chưa có thông tin cơ sở khám bệnh, chữa bệnh. Vui lòng liên hệ quản trị viên.”. EF-05 (at step 6): The browser cannot print5.1. The system shows MSG49. The audit entry stays, and the next attempt counts as a reprint. EF-06 (at any step): Session expired or system error6.1. If the session has expired, the system shows MSG12 and opens the Login screen.6.2. On a system or network error, the system shows MSG80 and the Doctor may retry. |  |  |
| **Postconditions** | Success: one PRINT entry is recorded in the audit log. No order, payment or queue data changes. Failure: nothing changes.  |  |  |
| **Business Rules** | BR-26; BR-120  |  |  |
| **Messages** | MSG12, MSG13, MSG39, MSG49, MSG80, MSG104  |  |  |

## **10\. Medical Record** {#10.-medical-record}

### **10.1 UC-51: View List Medical Record** {#10.1-uc-51:-view-list-medical-record}

| Primary Actors | Doctor | Secondary Actors | None |
| ----: | :---- | ----: | :---- |
| **Description** | As a Doctor, I want to search and view the list of medical records of patients, so that I can review their examination history. Doctors can view the medical records of all patients (BR-35). |  |  |
| **Preconditions** | 1\. The Doctor is signed in (UC-01). |  |  |
| **Normal Flow** | 1\. The Doctor selects Medical Records in the menu. 2\. The system shows the search box (patient code, citizen ID, name, phone) and filters: Visit date (From – To), Room, Diagnosis (ICD-10), Status (Completed, Abandoned, Active). 3\. The Doctor enters a keyword and/or filters. 4\. The system shows the matching patients: patient code, full name, date of birth, gender, number of visits, last visit date, last diagnosis. 5\. The Doctor selects a patient. 6\. The system shows the list of visits of the patient, newest first: registration code, date, room, doctor, visit type, final diagnosis (ICD-10), status. 7\. The Doctor selects a visit. *\=\>Continue in UC-52.* |  |  |
| **Alternative Flows** | **AF-01 (at step 1): Opened from the current visit** 1\. From the Current Visit Record (UC-47), the Doctor clicks History; the system opens step 6 for the patient of the visit. *\=\>Continue at step 6\.* |  |  |
| **Exception Flows** | **EF-01 (at step 4): No record matches** 1\. The system shows MSG01. *\=\>Return to step 3\.* **EF-02 (at step 1): The user is not a Doctor** 1\. The system shows MSG13. *\=\>The use case ends.* **EF-03 (any step): Session expired or system error** 1\. The system shows MSG12 or MSG99. *\=\>The use case ends.* |  |  |
| **Postconditions** | The medical records are listed. No data is changed. Every access to a patient's records is recorded in the audit log. |  |  |
| **Business Rules** | BR-35; Data rule: Medical data is access-controlled (I.3.3); Security: Medical data confidentiality (IV.2.3) |  |  |
| **Messages** | MSG01, MSG12, MSG13, MSG99 |  |  |

### **10.2 UC-52: View Medical Record Detail** {#10.2-uc-52:-view-medical-record-detail}

| Primary Actors | Doctor | Secondary Actors | None |
| ----: | :---- | ----: | :---- |
| **Description** | As a Doctor, I want to view the detail of a medical record, including the examination history and the paraclinical results of all visits, so that I can make decisions based on the patient's full history (BR-35). |  |  |
| **Preconditions** | 1\. The Doctor has selected a visit in UC-51, UC-34 or from the Current Visit Record (UC-47). |  |  |
| **Normal Flow** | 1\. The system shows the patient header: patient code, full name, age, gender, drug allergies (red label), medical history. 2\. The system shows the selected visit: registration code, date, room, doctor, visit type, priority, reason and initial symptoms, transfers (if any), vital signs, symptoms and findings, paraclinical orders with results and files (UC-55), final diagnosis (ICD-10) and conclusion, prescription, follow-up appointment, status and closed time. 3\. The Doctor can switch to another visit of the same patient with the visit timeline. 4\. The Doctor clicks a result file to open it; the system checks the Doctor's access before every download (Data rule: Medical data is access-controlled, I.3.3). 5\. The system shows the action Export Medical Record (UC-53). |  |  |
| **Alternative Flows** | **AF-01 (at step 2): The visit is the Doctor's current, unfinished visit** 1\. The system shows the Edit button, which opens the Current Visit Record (UC-47 / UC-56). Records of other visits are read-only (BR-35). *\=\>Continue at step 3\.* **AF-02 (at step 2): The visit is Abandoned** 1\. The system shows the data recorded before the visit was abandoned, marked "Abandoned – no conclusion" (BR-22). *\=\>Continue at step 3\.* |  |  |
| **Exception Flows** | **EF-01 (at step 2): The record does not exist** 1\. The system shows MSG41. *\=\>The use case ends.* **EF-02 (at step 4): The file cannot be loaded** 1\. The system shows MSG99. *\=\>Return to step 3\.* **EF-03 (any step): Session expired** 1\. The system shows MSG12. *\=\>The use case ends.* |  |  |
| **Postconditions** | The medical record is shown read-only (except the current unfinished visit). The access is recorded in the audit log. |  |  |
| **Business Rules** | BR-22, BR-32, BR-35; Data rule: Medical data is access-controlled (I.3.3) |  |  |
| **Messages** | MSG12, MSG41, MSG99 |  |  |

### **10.3 UC-53: Export Medical Record** {#10.3-uc-53:-export-medical-record}

| Primary Actors | Doctor | Secondary Actors | None |
| ----: | :---- | ----: | :---- |
| **Description** | As a Doctor, I want to export a medical record to a printable file, so that it can be printed or stored according to the hospital's needs. Doctors can export the records of all patients (BR-35). |  |  |
| **Preconditions** | 1\. The Doctor is viewing a medical record (UC-52). |  |  |
| **Normal Flow** | 1\. The Doctor clicks Export Medical Record. 2\. The system asks for the scope: Current visit only, or All visits of the patient. 3\. The Doctor selects the scope and confirms. 4\. The system creates a PDF file (SW-03) using the medical record layout (patient information, visits with vital signs, findings, paraclinical results, diagnosis, prescription, follow-up), with the hospital header, export time and exporting Doctor. 5\. The system downloads the file and shows MSG36. 6\. The system records the export in the audit log (patient, scope, Doctor, time). |  |  |
| **Alternative Flows** | **AF-01 (at step 3): The Doctor cancels** 1\. No file is created. *\=\>The use case ends.* **AF-02 (at step 4): The visit is not closed yet** 1\. The file is marked "Draft – visit not completed". *\=\>Continue at step 5\.* |  |  |
| **Exception Flows** | **EF-01 (at step 4): The file cannot be created** 1\. The system shows MSG99. *\=\>Return to step 2\.* **EF-02 (any step): Session expired** 1\. The system shows MSG12. *\=\>The use case ends.* |  |  |
| **Postconditions** | The file is downloaded and the export is logged. No data in the system is changed. |  |  |
| **Business Rules** | BR-32, BR-35; Security: Audit trail (IV.2.3); OR-01 |  |  |
| **Messages** | MSG12, MSG36, MSG99 |  |  |

## **11\. Examination Conclusion** {#11.-examination-conclusion}

### **11.1 UC-54: View Paraclinical Order List** {#11.1-uc-54:-view-paraclinical-order-list}

| Primary Actors | Doctor | Secondary Actors | None |
| ----: | :---- | ----: | :---- |
| **Description** | As a Doctor, I want to see the paraclinical services I ordered for a patient’s visit, and search and filter them, so that I can follow their status and open each result in detail. |  |  |
| **Preconditions** | The Doctor is signed in (UC-01). The Doctor is assigned to an examination room (BR-05). The Doctor has selected a patient from the room’s waiting lists (UC-43) and opened the visit. |  |  |
| **Normal Flow** | The Doctor opens the “Chỉ định cận lâm sàng” tab of the visit. The system shows the search box and filters: status, service group The system shows the order slips of the visit, newest first. Under each slip, the system lists its orders. For each order it shows: Mã chỉ định, Tên dịch vụ, Phòng thực hiện, Giá, Trạng thái, Xem chi tiết, Huỷ |  |  |
| **Alternative Flows** | AF-01 (at step 2): The Doctor searches or filters	 1.1. The Doctor enters a keyword (order code or service name, BR-110) and/or selects a status or service group. 1.2. The system shows only matching orders and hides slips with no matching order. 1.3. Continue at step 4\. AF-02 (at step 2): No order matches 2.1. The system shows MSG01. 2.2. Continue at step 2\. AF-03 (at step 3): The visit has no order slip 3.1. The system shows MSG92. 3.2. The use case ends. AF-04 (at step 4): The Doctor views an order’s result 4.1. “Xem chi tiết” is available only on orders with status “Đã có kết quả”. 4.2. The Doctor clicks “Xem chi tiết”. 4.3. The use case continues in UC-55. AF-05 (at step 4): The Doctor cancels a refused service 5.1. “Hủy” is shown only on orders that can still be cancelled: not yet paid (service visit) or not yet accepted by a technician (BHYT visit) (BR-25). 5.2. The Doctor clicks “Hủy”. 5.3. The use case continues in UC-76. |  |  |
| **Exception Flows** | EF-01 (at step 1): The user is not a Doctor 1.1. The system shows MSG13. 1.2. The use case ends. EF-02 (at step 1): The Doctor is not assigned to any room 2.1. The system shows MSG99. 2.2. The use case ends. EF-03 (at any step): Session expired or system error 3.1. The system shows MSG12 (session expired) or MSG80 (system error); nothing is changed. 3.2. The use case ends. |  |  |
| **Postconditions** | The paraclinical orders of the visit are shown. No data is changed |  |  |
| **Business Rules** | BR-02, BR-05, BR-09, BR-110 |  |  |
| **Messages** | MSG01, MSG12, MSG13, MSG80, MSG92, MSG99 |  |  |

### **11.3 UC-56: Conclude Examination** {#11.3-uc-56:-conclude-examination}

| Primary Actors | Doctor | Secondary Actors | None |
| ----: | :---- | ----: | :---- |
| **Description** | As a Doctor, I want to record the final diagnosis with ICD-10 codes, the treatment plan and advice, then confirm the conclusion, so that the visit is completed and its record is closed. |  |  |
| **Preconditions** | The Doctor is signed in (UC-01), assigned to the examination room and working the current shift (BR-05, BR-19, BR-55). The visit belongs to the Doctor’s room and its medical record has not been closed (BR-32, BR-35). The “Kết luận & Hẹn tái khám” tab is enabled: every non-cancelled paraclinical order has a result, the patient refused paraclinical services, or no service was ordered (BR-30, BR-41). |  |  |
| **Normal Flow** | The Doctor opens the “Kết luận & Hẹn tái khám” tab of the visit. The system checks permission, assigned room, shift and record status (BR-02, BR-05, BR-19, BR-32, BR-55). The system shows the preliminary diagnosis from UC-47 for reference and the conclusion form with any saved data (BR-106): Chẩn đoán\*, Bệnh chính (ICD-10), Bệnh kèm theo (ICD-10), Hướng điều trị, Kết quả điều trị\* (Khỏi, Đỡ, Không thay đổi, Nặng hơn), Lời dặn\*, Tóm tắt bệnh án, Ghi chú. The Doctor fills in the form. ICD-10 codes are searched by code or name among active codes; each selected code is saved with its name at the time of selection (BR-31, BR-46). The Doctor clicks “Lưu kết luận”. The system validates the input (BR-31, BR-51, BR-106). The system saves the conclusion with the responsible Doctor and time, records the audit log with before/after values (BR-42), and shows MSG03. The record stays open. |  |  |
| **Alternative Flows** | AF-01 (at step 4): The main diagnosis code is discouraged 1.1. The system shows MSG66 (BR-51). 1.2. The Doctor keeps the code or selects another one. AF-02 (at step 3): The conclusion was saved before 2.1. The system shows the saved conclusion in the form. 2.2. If a prescription has been submitted successfully, “Bệnh chính” and “Bệnh kèm theo” are read-only, because they were sent with the prescription (BR-47); the other fields can still be edited. 2.3. The use case continues at step 4\. AF-03 (at step 4): Leave with unsaved changes 3.1. The Doctor leaves the tab; the system shows MSG38. 3.2. If the Doctor selects “Tiếp tục chỉnh sửa”, the use case returns to step 4\. 3.3. If the Doctor selects “Loại bỏ”, unsaved changes are discarded, saved data is kept and the use case ends. |  |  |
| **Exception Flows** | EF-01 (at step 2): No permission, or outside the assigned room or shift 1.1. The system shows MSG13 or MSG48 and prevents updates. 1.2. The use case ends. EF-02 (at step 2): The medical record is already closed 2.1. The system shows MSG68. 2.2. The use case ends. EF-03 (at step 4): Inactive ICD-10 code 3.1. The system prevents the selection and shows MSG40. 3.2. The use case returns to step 4\. EF-04 (at step 6): A required field is empty or an input is too long 4.1. The system shows MSG02 or MSG08. 4.2. The use case returns to step 4\. EF-05 (at step 6): The main diagnosis is missing, duplicated or not allowed 5.1. If there is no main diagnosis or more than one, the system shows MSG64. If the code cannot be used as a main diagnosis, the system shows MSG65 (BR-51). 5.2. The use case returns to step 4\. EF-06 (at any step): Session expired or system error 6.1. The system shows MSG12 or MSG80; nothing is saved. 6.2. The use case ends. |  |  |
| **Postconditions** | Success: the conclusion is saved in the visit’s medical record and recorded in the audit log. The record stays open for prescribing (UC-59, UC-90), follow-up (UC-61) and closing (UC-58). Failure or cancel: invalid data is not saved; previously saved data is kept. |  |  |
| **Business Rules** | BR-02, BR-05, BR-19, BR-30, BR-31, BR-32, BR-41, BR-42, BR-46, BR-47, BR-51, BR-55, BR-106 |  |  |
| **Messages** | MSG02, MSG03, MSG08, MSG12, MSG13, MSG38, MSG40, MSG48, MSG64, MSG65, MSG66, MSG68, MSG75, MSG80 |  |  |

The use case continues at step 2\. AF-02 (at step 3): Close the preview 2.1. The Doctor closes the preview; nothing is printed. 2.2. The use case ends. |  |  |
| **Exception Flows** | EF-01 (at step 1): The conclusion is not confirmed yet 1.1. The system shows MSG61. 1.2. The use case ends. EF-02 (at step 4): The printer fails 2.1. The system shows MSG49. 2.2. The use case returns to step 2\. EF-03 (at any step): Session expired or system error 3.1. The system shows MSG12 or MSG80. 3.2. The use case ends. |  |  |

| **Business Rules** | BR-02, BR-31, BR-32, BR-35 |  |  |

### **11.5 UC-58: Close Medical Record** {#11.5-uc-58:-close-medical-record}

| Primary Actors | Doctor | Secondary Actors | None |
| ----: | :---- | ----: | :---- |
| **Description** | As a Doctor, I want to confirm the conclusion and close the medical record in one action, so that the visit is completed, the record is locked and archived, and remaining charges go to the cashier (BR-32). |  |  |
| **Preconditions** | The Doctor is signed in (UC-01), assigned to the examination room and working the current shift (BR-05, BR-19, BR-55). The conclusion of the visit has been saved (UC-56); otherwise “Xác nhận kết luận” is disabled. The medical record has not been closed. |  |  |
| **Normal Flow** | The Doctor clicks “Xác nhận kết luận”. The system checks that every non-cancelled paraclinical order has a result (BR-30), the prescription, if any, has been accepted by the national prescription system (BR-47), and the follow-up appointment, if any, has been created (BR-32). The system shows MSG27. The Doctor confirms. In one transaction, the system fixes the coverage rate and recalculates pending charges (BR-27), locks the conclusion and follow-up appointment, sets the visit to “Hoàn thành” with the closing time, and records the audit log (BR-42). For a BHYT visit, pending charges stay “Chờ thu” and appear in the cashier’s list (UC-69); charges whose patient amount is 0 become “Miễn phí” (BR-15, BR-37). The system creates the archive record: archive number, data package, hash and retention date (BR-44, BR-126). The system removes the visit from the room’s lists and shows MSG03. |  |  |
| **Alternative Flows** | AF-01 (at step 4): The Doctor does not confirm 1.1. The Doctor clicks “Hủy” in MSG27; nothing is changed and the record stays open. 1.2. The use case ends. |  |  |
| **Exception Flows** | EF-01 (at step 1): No permission, or outside the assigned room or shift 1.1. The system shows MSG13 or MSG48. 1.2. The use case ends. EF-02 (at step 2): Some paraclinical orders have no result 2.1. The system shows MSG25. 2.2. The use case ends. EF-03 (at step 2): The prescription or follow-up appointment is not completed 3.1. The system shows MSG67. 3.2. The use case ends. EF-04 (at any step): Session expired or system error 4.1. The system shows MSG12 or MSG80; the whole transaction is rolled back and the record stays open. 4.2. The use case ends. |  |  |
| **Postconditions** | Success: the conclusion is confirmed; the visit is “Hoàn thành”; the record is locked, cannot be edited (BR-32, BR-35) and is archived (BR-126); BHYT charges wait for payment at the cashier (BR-15). Failure or cancel: nothing is changed; the record stays open. |  |  |
| **Business Rules** | BR-02, BR-05, BR-15, BR-19, BR-27, BR-30, BR-32, BR-35, BR-37, BR-42, BR-44, BR-47, BR-55, BR-126 |  |  |
| **Messages** | MSG03, MSG12, MSG13, MSG25, MSG27, MSG48, MSG67, MSG75, MSG80 |  |  |

### **11.6 UC-59: Prescribe Medication** {#11.6-uc-59:-prescribe-medication}

| Primary Actors | Doctor | Secondary Actors | None |
| ----: | :---- | ----: | :---- |
| **Description** | As a Doctor, I want to create an electronic prescription from the medicine catalog, so that it can be submitted to the national prescription system and printed for the patient. The facility does not sell or dispense medication; receipts never include drug costs (BR-33). |  |  |
| **Preconditions** | The Doctor is signed in (UC-01), assigned to the examination room and working the current shift (BR-05, BR-19, BR-55). The conclusion of the visit has been saved (UC-56) and the medical record is not closed (BR-32). |  |  |
| **Normal Flow** | The Doctor opens the “Đơn thuốc” tab of the visit. The system checks permission, room, shift, record status and that the Doctor has a prescriber link code (BR-49, BR-65). The system shows the saved diagnosis and the patient’s drug allergies (BR-23), and the prescription form. Each drug line has: “Thuốc”, “Liều mỗi lần”, “Số lần/ngày”, “Số ngày”, “Số lượng”, “Cách dùng”. The prescription also has “Lưu ý” and “Lời dặn”. The Doctor selects drugs from the active catalog (only “Thông thường” drugs with a BYT code are shown – BR-33) and fills in each line. The Doctor clicks “Lưu”. The system checks the input (BR-107): at least one drug line; no drug repeated; “Số lần/ngày” 1–24; “Số ngày” 1–30, or up to 90 when the main or a secondary diagnosis is in Appendix VII of Circular 26/2025/TT-BYT; “Số lượng” greater than 0 and at most 9,999. The system checks the drugs against the recorded allergies (BR-23). The system saves the prescription (one per visit – BR-33). On the first save, it generates the prescription code (BR-52). The change is recorded in the audit log (BR-42). The system shows MSG03. The Doctor can submit the prescription (UC-90). |  |  |
| **Alternative Flows** | AF-01 (at step 7): A drug matches a recorded allergy 1.1. The system shows MSG26. 1.2. If the Doctor continues, the use case continues at step 8\. 1.3. If the Doctor cancels, the use case returns to step 4 to change the drug. AF-02 (at step 3): The visit already has a prescription 2.1. The system shows the saved prescription for editing; the prescription code does not change (BR-52). 2.2. The use case continues at step 4\. AF-03 (at step 4): Remove a drug line 3.1. The Doctor clicks “Xóa” on a line; the system removes it. 3.2. The use case returns to step 4\. AF-04 (at step 4): Cancel 4.1. The Doctor clicks “Hủy”; if there are unsaved changes, the system shows MSG38. 4.2. If the Doctor selects “Tiếp tục chỉnh sửa”, the use case returns to step 4\. 4.3. If the Doctor selects “Loại bỏ”, unsaved changes are discarded and the use case ends. |  |  |
| **Exception Flows** | EF-01 (at step 2): No permission, or outside the assigned room or shift 1.1. The system shows MSG13 or MSG48. 1.2. The use case ends. EF-02 (at step 2): The medical record is closed 2.1. The system shows MSG68. 2.2. The use case ends. EF-03 (at step 2): The Doctor has no prescriber link code 3.1. The system shows MSG87. 3.2. The use case ends. EF-04 (at step 2): The prescription has already been submitted successfully 4.1. The system shows the prescription read-only and MSG88 (BR-47). 4.2. The use case ends. EF-05 (at step 4): The drug is inactive or not in the “Thông thường” group 5.1. The system shows MSG40. 5.2. The use case returns to step 4\. EF-06 (at step 6): A required field is empty, a value is invalid or too long 6.1. The system shows MSG02, MSG05 or MSG08. 6.2. The use case returns to step 4\. EF-07 (at step 6): The same drug is selected twice 7.1. The system shows MSG89. 7.2. The use case returns to step 4\. EF-08 (at step 8): The prescription was changed by another user 8.1. The system shows MSG75; nothing is saved. 8.2. The use case returns to step 3 after reloading. EF-09 (at any step): Session expired or system error 9.1. The system shows MSG12 or MSG80; nothing is saved. 9.2. The use case ends. |  |  |
| **Postconditions** | Success: the visit has one saved prescription with a unique code, ready to be submitted (UC-90). No receipt is created for medication (BR-33). Failure or cancel: no change is saved. |  |  |
| **Business Rules** | BR-02, BR-05, BR-19, BR-23, BR-32, BR-33, BR-42, BR-47, BR-49, BR-52, BR-55, BR-65, BR-107, BR-119 |  |  |
| **Messages** | MSG02, MSG03, MSG05, MSG08, MSG12, MSG13, MSG26, MSG38, MSG40, MSG48, MSG68, MSG75, MSG80, MSG87, MSG88, MSG89 |  |  |

### **11.7 UC-60: Print Prescription** {#11.7-uc-60:-print-prescription}

| Primary Actors | Doctor | Secondary Actors | None |
| ----: | :---- | ----: | :---- |
| **Description** | As a Doctor, I want to print the submitted prescription with its code, so that the patient can buy the medication outside the facility (BR-33). |  |  |
| **Preconditions** | The Doctor is signed in (UC-01). The prescription of the visit has been submitted successfully (UC-90). |  |  |
| **Normal Flow** | The Doctor clicks “In đơn thuốc”. The system shows a preview of the prescription: facility information (UC-77), prescription code (BR-52), patient information (name, age, gender, address, insurance card number if any), main and secondary diagnoses with ICD-10 codes, drug lines, notes and advice, follow-up date if any, and the Doctor’s academic title and full name. The Doctor clicks “In”. The system sends the prescription to the printer. |  |  |

The use case continues at step 2\. AF-02 (at step 3): Close the preview 2.1. The Doctor closes the preview; nothing is printed. 2.2. The use case ends. |  |  |
| **Exception Flows** | EF-01 (at step 1): The prescription has not been submitted successfully 1.1. The system shows MSG90. 1.2. The use case ends. EF-02 (at step 4): The printer fails 2.1. The system shows MSG49. 2.2. The use case returns to step 2\. EF-03 (at any step): Session expired or system error 3.1. The system shows MSG12 or MSG80. 3.2. The use case ends. |  |  |
| **Postconditions** | The prescription is printed. No data is changed. |  |  |
| **Business Rules** | BR-02, BR-33, BR-47, BR-52 |  |  |
| **Messages** | MSG12, MSG49, MSG80, MSG90 |  |  |

### **11.8 UC-61: Create Follow-up Appointment** {#11.8-uc-61:-create-follow-up-appointment}

| Primary Actors | Doctor | Secondary Actors | None |
| ----: | :---- | ----: | :---- |
| **Description** | As a Doctor, I want to set a follow-up date and advice for a patient who needs periodic monitoring, so that the patient comes back on time. Each visit has at most one appointment; it is used once, within its validity period (BR-34). |  |  |
| **Preconditions** | The Doctor is signed in (UC-01), assigned to the examination room and working the current shift (BR-05, BR-19, BR-55). The medical record of the visit is not closed (BR-32). |  |  |

The system shows the form: “Ngày tái khám”\*, “Lời dặn tái khám”. The Doctor fills in the form and clicks “Lưu”. The system checks the input (BR-108): the date is after the visit date and at most 365 days later; the advice is at most 2,000 characters. The system saves the appointment with status “Đã hẹn”, linked to the visit and the patient, generates the appointment slip number (BR-53) and records the audit log (BR-42). The system shows MSG04. |  |  |
| **Alternative Flows** | AF-01 (at step 3): The visit already has an appointment 1.1. The system shows the saved appointment for editing. 1.2. The Doctor changes it and clicks “Lưu”; the use case continues at step 5\. 1.3. If the prescription has already been submitted, the new date does not change the date on the submitted prescription (BR-47). AF-02 (at step 4): Cancel 2.1. The Doctor clicks “Hủy”; if there are unsaved changes, the system shows MSG38. 2.2. If the Doctor selects “Tiếp tục chỉnh sửa”, the use case returns to step 4\. 2.3. If the Doctor selects “Loại bỏ”, unsaved changes are discarded and the use case ends. |  |  |
| **Exception Flows** | EF-01 (at step 2): No permission, or outside the assigned room or shift 1.1. The system shows MSG13 or MSG48. 1.2. The use case ends. EF-02 (at step 2): The medical record is closed 2.1. The system shows MSG68. 2.2. The use case ends. EF-03 (at step 5): The date is empty 3.1. The system shows MSG02. 3.2. The use case returns to step 4\. EF-04 (at step 5): The date is not after the visit date, or more than 365 days later 4.1. The system shows MSG33 or MSG05. 4.2. The use case returns to step 4\. EF-05 (at step 5): The advice is too long 5.1. The system shows MSG08. 5.2. The use case returns to step 4\. EF-06 (at any step): Session expired or system error 6.1. The system shows MSG12 or MSG80; nothing is saved. 6.2. The use case ends. |  |  |
| **Postconditions** | Success: the visit has one appointment with status “Đã hẹn” and a unique slip number. It is locked when the record is closed (UC-58) and can be used at reception from the follow-up date until the end of its validity period (BR-34, BR-124). Failure or cancel: no change is saved. |  |  |
| **Business Rules** | BR-02, BR-05, BR-19, BR-32, BR-34, BR-42, BR-47, BR-53, BR-55, BR-108, BR-124 |  |  |
| **Messages** | MSG02, MSG04, MSG05, MSG08, MSG12, MSG13, MSG33, MSG38, MSG48, MSG68, MSG80 |  |  |

## **12\. Paraclinical Service** {#12.-paraclinical-service}

### **12.1 UC-63: View Waiting Paraclinical List** {#12.1-uc-63:-view-waiting-paraclinical-list}

| Primary Actors | Technician | Secondary Actors | None |
| ----: | :---- | ----: | :---- |
| **Description** | As a Technician, I want to see the waiting list of paid (or fee-exempt) paraclinical services routed to my room, so that I know which patient to call next. Orders only reach the room after payment is confirmed or if the patient amount is 0 (BR-26), are routed to the active room with the fewest waiting patients (BR-28) and are ordered by priority first, then registration time (BR-18). |  |  |
| **Preconditions** | 1\. The Technician is signed in and is assigned to an Active paraclinical room (UC-15). |  |  |
| **Normal Flow** | 1\. The Technician opens the Technician Dashboard (home screen after sign-in) or selects Paraclinical Waiting List. 2\. The system shows the room name and the tabs: Waiting (default), Skipped (UC-45), Pending Result (UC-64). 3\. The system shows the orders of this room with status Waiting: patient name, age, gender, priority mark, service, ordering Doctor and room, clinical note, released time, registration time. 4\. The system orders the list: priority patients first, then by registration time of the visit (BR-18). 5\. The system refreshes the list automatically at least every 10 seconds (UI-04). 6\. The Technician clicks Call Next or Call on an order. *\=\>Continue in UC-65.* |  |  |
| **Alternative Flows** | **AF-01 (at step 3): The list is empty** 1\. The system shows MSG01. *\=\>Continue at step 5\.* **AF-02 (at step 3): An order is In Progress by another technician of the room** 1\. The system shows it in a separate "In progress" section with the technician's name. *\=\>Continue at step 4\.* |  |  |
| **Exception Flows** | **EF-01 (at step 1): The Technician is not assigned to any room** 1\. The system shows MSG50 and an empty list. *\=\>The use case ends.* **EF-02 (any step): Session expired or system error** 1\. The system shows MSG12 or MSG99 and keeps the last loaded list. *\=\>The use case ends.* |  |  |
| **Postconditions** | The Technician sees the ordered waiting list of their room. No data is changed. |  |  |
| **Business Rules** | BR-14, BR-18, BR-19, BR-26, BR-28; UI-04 |  |  |
| **Messages** | MSG01, MSG12, MSG50, MSG99 |  |  |

### **12.2 UC-64: View Pending Result List** {#12.2-uc-64:-view-pending-result-list}

| Primary Actors | Technician | Secondary Actors | None |
| ----: | :---- | ----: | :---- |
| **Description** | As a Technician, I want to see the services I have performed whose results are not submitted yet, ordered by performed time, so that I do not forget to enter and submit any result. |  |  |
| **Preconditions** | 1\. The Technician is signed in and is assigned to an Active paraclinical room. |  |  |
| **Normal Flow** | 1\. The Technician opens the Pending Result tab. 2\. The system shows the orders performed by this Technician (status Performed, result not submitted – BR-29): patient name, service, performed time, draft saved (Yes/No), ordering Doctor. 3\. The system orders the list by performed time, earliest first. 4\. The Technician selects an order. *\=\>Continue in UC-67.* |  |  |
| **Alternative Flows** | **AF-01 (at step 2): The list is empty** 1\. The system shows MSG01. *\=\>The use case ends.* **AF-02 (at step 2): Show the whole room** 1\. The Technician selects "All technicians of the room"; the list is read-only for orders performed by others (only the performer can record the result – BR-29). *\=\>Continue at step 3\.* |  |  |
| **Exception Flows** | **EF-01 (at step 1): The Technician is not assigned to any room** 1\. The system shows MSG50. *\=\>The use case ends.* **EF-02 (any step): Session expired or system error** 1\. The system shows MSG12 or MSG99. *\=\>The use case ends.* |  |  |
| **Postconditions** | The pending results of the Technician are shown. No data is changed. |  |  |
| **Business Rules** | BR-19, BR-29 |  |  |
| **Messages** | MSG01, MSG12, MSG50, MSG99 |  |  |

### **12.3 UC-65: Accept Paraclinical Order** {#12.3-uc-65:-accept-paraclinical-order}

| Primary Actors | Technician | Secondary Actors | None |
| ----: | :---- | ----: | :---- |
| **Description** | As a Technician, I want to call the next paid service in my room and accept it if the patient is present, so that I can start performing it; if the patient is absent, the order moves to the skipped list (BR-20, BR-21). Only paid or fee-exempt orders can be accepted (BR-26). |  |  |
| **Preconditions** | 1\. The Technician is viewing the waiting list of their room (UC-63) and it contains at least one order. |  |  |
| **Normal Flow** | 1\. The Technician clicks Call Next (first order of the list) or Call on a selected order. 2\. The system checks that the order is still Waiting, routed to this room, and that its receipt is Paid (or fee-exempt) (BR-26). 3\. The system announces the call (queue display HW-04) and marks the order "Calling". 4\. The patient comes into the room with the order slip. 5\. The Technician clicks Accept. 6\. The system sets the order to In Progress, assigns it to the Technician (performer) with the start time and records it in the audit log. 7\. The system shows the order detail (patient, service, clinical note, allergies) and the action Confirm Performed (UC-66). |  |  |
| **Alternative Flows** | **AF-01 (at step 4): The patient is absent** 1\. The Technician clicks Absent. 2\. The system sets the order to Skipped, records the skip time and adds it to the room's skipped list ordered by skip time (BR-21); the system shows MSG58. *\=\>Return to step 1\.* **AF-02 (at step 4): The patient does not respond the first time** 1\. The Technician clicks Call Again. *\=\>Return to step 4\.* **AF-03 (at step 6): The patient also has orders in other rooms** 1\. The system shows the other orders and their rooms so that the Technician can tell the patient where to go next. *\=\>Continue at step 7\.* |  |  |
| **Exception Flows** | **EF-01 (at step 2): The order is not paid** 1\. The system shows MSG28 and does not accept it. *\=\>The use case ends.* **EF-02 (at step 2): The order was already called or accepted by another technician** 1\. The system shows MSG23 and refreshes the list. *\=\>Return to step 1\.* **EF-03 (at step 6): Session expired or system errorr** 1\. The system shows MSG12 or MSG99; the order stays Waiting. *\=\>The use case ends.* |  |  |
| **Postconditions** | Present: the order is In Progress and assigned to the Technician. Absent: the order is Skipped until the patient returns (UC-46) or the day ends; at the end of the day it is cancelled and the visit becomes Abandoned (BR-22). |  |  |
| **Business Rules** | BR-18, BR-19, BR-20, BR-21, BR-22, BR-26 |  |  |
| **Messages** | MSG12, MSG23, MSG28, MSG58, MSG99 |  |  |

### **12.4 UC-66: Perform Paraclinical Order** {#12.4-uc-66:-perform-paraclinical-order}

| Primary Actors | Technician | Secondary Actors | None |
| ----: | :---- | ----: | :---- |
| **Description** | As a Technician, I want to confirm that the accepted service has been performed, so that the order status is updated and the result can be entered. The service itself (ultrasound, X-ray, CT, MRI, endoscopy, ECG, laboratory tests) is performed with the equipment outside the system; results are entered manually (SW-04). |  |  |
| **Preconditions** | 1\. The order is In Progress and assigned to the Technician (UC-65 or UC-46). |  |  |
| **Normal Flow** | 1\. The Technician performs the service with the patient (with the paraclinical doctor where required, e.g. ultrasound or endoscopy teams). 2\. The Technician clicks Confirm Performed on the order. 3\. The system sets the order to Performed with the performed time and adds it to the Technician's pending result list (UC-64). 4\. The system shows MSG03 and the action Record Result (UC-67). 5\. The patient goes to the next paraclinical room if the visit has other orders, or waits for the results and then returns to the original Doctor. |  |  |
| **Alternative Flows** | **AF-01 (at step 2): The result can be entered right away (e.g. ECG)** 1\. The Technician clicks Record Result directly; the system sets the order to Performed. *\=\>Continue in UC-67.* **AF-02 (at step 1): The service cannot be performed (patient not prepared, equipment problem)** 1\. The Technician clicks Return to Waiting with a reason; the order goes back to Waiting at its original place and the reason is recorded. *\=\>The use case ends.* |  |  |
| **Exception Flows** | **EF-01 (at step 2): The order is not assigned to this Technician** 1\. The system shows MSG13. *\=\>The use case ends.* **EF-02 (at step 3): Session expired or system error** 1\. The system shows MSG12 or MSG99; the order stays In Progress. *\=\>The use case ends.* |  |  |
| **Postconditions** | Success: the order is Performed and waits for its result. Failure: the order stays In Progress. |  |  |
| **Business Rules** | BR-19, BR-29 |  |  |
| **Messages** | MSG03, MSG12, MSG13, MSG99 |  |  |

### **12.5 UC-67: Record Paraclinical Result** {#12.5-uc-67:-record-paraclinical-result}

| Primary Actors | Technician | Secondary Actors | Cloudinary Upload API (result files) |
| ----: | :---- | ----: | :---- |
| **Description** | As a Technician, I want to enter, review and submit the result of a service I performed (content, conclusion, files), so that it is attached to the patient's medical record and sent to the examining Doctor. A Technician can only record results for services they performed, and a submitted result cannot be edited (BR-29). |  |  |
| **Preconditions** | 1\. The order is Performed (or In Progress, UC-66 AF-01) and the Technician is its performer. |  |  |
| **Normal Flow** | 1\. The Technician opens the order from the pending result list (UC-64). 2\. The system shows the result form: patient and service information, Result content\* (values with units and reference ranges for lab tests, description for imaging and functional tests), Result conclusion\*, Attached files (images or PDF, at most 10 files, each at most 20 MB). 3\. The Technician enters the result and uploads the files. 4\. The system uploads the files to the file storage (Cloudinary Upload API) and keeps their protected links. 5\. The Technician clicks Save draft to review, then Submit. 6\. The system checks the required fields and file types/sizes. 7\. The system shows MSG06 warning that the result cannot be edited after submission. 8\. The Technician confirms. 9\. The system saves and locks the result, sets the order to Completed, attaches the result to the medical record of the visit and records it in the audit log (BR-29). 10\. The system checks whether every order of the visit has a result; if so, the visit becomes Waiting for Conclusion, appears in the conclusion waiting list of the original room and the Doctor is notified (BR-18, BR-28; background job 8). 11\. The system shows MSG29 and the action Print Result (UC-68). |  |  |
| **Alternative Flows** | **AF-01 (at step 5): Save draft only** 1\. The system saves the draft without locking it; the order stays in the pending result list. *\=\>The use case ends.* **AF-02 (at step 10): Other orders of the visit are still not completed** 1\. The visit stays Waiting for Paraclinical; the Doctor sees the progress (UC-54). *\=\>Continue at step 11\.* |  |  |
| **Exception Flows** | **EF-01 (at step 6): Required field empty, wrong file type or file too large** 1\. The system shows MSG02 or MSG05. *\=\>Return to step 3\.* **EF-02 (at step 4): The upload fails** 1\. The system shows MSG99; the entered text is kept and the Technician can upload again. *\=\>Return to step 3\.* **EF-03 (at step 1): The Technician is not the performer** 1\. The form is read-only and the system shows MSG13. *\=\>The use case ends.* **EF-04 (at step 1): The result was already submitted** 1\. The system shows MSG61; the result is read-only. *\=\>The use case ends.* **EF-05 (at step 9): Session expired or system error** 1\. The system shows MSG12 or MSG99; the result is not submitted. *\=\>Return to step 5\.* |  |  |
| **Postconditions** | Success: the result is locked and attached to the medical record; the order is Completed; when all orders are completed the visit is Waiting for Conclusion and the Doctor is notified. Failure: the result is not submitted (a draft may be saved). |  |  |
| **Business Rules** | BR-18, BR-19, BR-28, BR-29; Data rules: One result per order item, Medical data is access-controlled (I.3.3); SW-04 |  |  |
| **Messages** | MSG02, MSG05, MSG06, MSG12, MSG13, MSG29, MSG61, MSG99 |  |  |

### **12.6 UC-68: Print Paraclinical Result** {#12.6-uc-68:-print-paraclinical-result}

| Primary Actors | Technician | Secondary Actors | None |
| ----: | :---- | ----: | :---- |
| **Description** | As a Technician, I want to print the paraclinical result for the patient, so that the patient keeps a paper copy of the result. |  |  |
| **Preconditions** | 1\. The result of the order has been submitted (UC-67). |  |  |
| **Normal Flow** | 1\. The Technician clicks Print Result. 2\. The system builds the result form (PF-03): hospital name, patient information, registration code, service, ordering Doctor, result content, images (if any), result conclusion, Technician (and paraclinical doctor), performed and submitted time. 3\. The system sends the form to the office printer (HW-02) and shows a preview. 4\. The Technician hands the result to the patient. |  |  |
| **Alternative Flows** | **AF-01 (at step 1): Reprint** 1\. The Technician opens the completed order from the room's history and prints; the form is marked "Copy". *\=\>Continue at step 3\.* |  |  |
| **Exception Flows** | **EF-01 (at step 1): The result is not submitted yet** 1\. The Print button is disabled (drafts cannot be printed). *\=\>The use case ends.* **EF-02 (at step 3): The printer fails** 1\. The system shows MSG52. *\=\>The use case ends.* |  |  |
| **Postconditions** | The patient receives the printed result. No data is changed (the print is logged). |  |  |
| **Business Rules** | BR-29 |  |  |
| **Messages** | MSG52 |  |  |

## **13\. Payment** {#13.-payment}

### **13.1 UC-69: View Waiting Payment List** {#13.1-uc-69:-view-waiting-payment-list}

| Primary Actors | Cashier | Secondary Actors | None |
| ----: | :---- | ----: | :---- |
| **Description** | As a Cashier, I want to see the pending receipts created automatically by the system — examination fee receipts at registration and paraclinical receipts when a Doctor confirms an order — so that I can collect the fees of the patients at the counter. Receipts are generated by the system; the Cashier cannot create them manually (BR-36). |  |  |
| **Preconditions** | 1\. The Cashier is signed in (UC-01). |  |  |
| **Normal Flow** | 1\. The Cashier opens the Cashier Dashboard (home screen after sign-in) or selects Waiting Payment List. 2\. The system shows the receipts with status Pending: receipt number, type (Examination fee / Paraclinical fee), registration code, patient code and name, priority mark, visit type and coverage rate, created time, total amount, insurance amount, patient amount (BR-27). 3\. The system orders the list by created time (priority patients highlighted) and refreshes it automatically (UI-04). 4\. The Cashier filters by type or searches (UC-70) for the patient at the counter. 5\. The Cashier selects a receipt. *\=\>Continue in UC-71.* |  |  |
| **Alternative Flows** | **AF-01 (at step 2): The list is empty** 1\. The system shows MSG01. *\=\>The use case ends.* |  |  |
| **Exception Flows** | **EF-01 (at step 1): The user is not a Cashier** 1\. The system shows MSG13. *\=\>The use case ends.* **EF-02 (any step): Session expired or system error** 1\. The system shows MSG12 or MSG99. *\=\>The use case ends.* |  |  |
| **Postconditions** | The pending receipts are shown. No data is changed. Receipts still Pending at the end of the day are cancelled by the end-of-day job (BR-22). |  |  |
| **Business Rules** | BR-15, BR-22, BR-26, BR-27, BR-36, BR-37; Permission Matrix 4.4 (Invoice) |  |  |
| **Messages** | MSG01, MSG12, MSG13, MSG99 |  |  |

### **13.2 UC-70: Search Payment** {#13.2-uc-70:-search-payment}

| Primary Actors | Cashier | Secondary Actors | None |
| ----: | :---- | ----: | :---- |
| **Description** | As a Cashier, I want to search for a receipt by receipt number, patient name or code, or registration code, so that I can quickly find the receipt of the patient at the counter or answer a question about a past payment.  |  |  |
| **Preconditions** | 1\. The Cashier is signed in (UC-01).  |  |  |
| **Normal Flow** | 1\. The Cashier enters a keyword in the search box of the payment management screen, and may choose a status, a type and a date range. 2\. The system validates the keyword (at least 2 characters) and the date range (from date not after to date – BR-111). 3\. The system searches all receipts (Pending, Paid, Exempt, Cancelled) by receipt code (HD…), receipt number (PT…), registration code, patient code (case-insensitive) or patient name (case- and accent-insensitive – BR-110), with the optional filters status, type and creation date range. 4\. The system shows the matching receipts: receipt code / visit, patient, payment type, amount to collect, status. 5\. The Cashier selects a receipt: a Pending receipt opens Confirm Payment (UC-71); a Paid receipt opens its detail with Print (UC-72); a Cancelled receipt opens read-only.  |  |  |
| **Alternative Flows** | **AF-01 (at step 4): Exactly one Pending receipt matches the registration code** 1\. The system opens the receipt detail with Confirm Payment (UC-71) directly. \=\> The use case ends.  |  |  |
| **Exception Flows** | ***EF-01 (at step 2): Keyword too short or start date after end date** 1\. The system shows MSG05 under the search box, or MSG50 for the date range, and does not search. \=\> Return to step 1\. **EF-02 (at step 4): No receipt matches** 1\. The system shows MSG01. \=\> Return to step 1\. **EF-03 (any step): Session expired or system error** 1\. The system shows MSG12 or MSG80. \=\> The use case ends..* |  |  |
| **Postconditions** | The matching receipts are shown. No data is changed. |  |  |
| **Business Rules** | BR-36, BR-37, BR-110, BR-111  |  |  |
| **Messages** | MSG01, MSG05, MSG12, MSG50, MSG80  |  |  |

### **13.3 UC-71: Confirm Payment** {#13.3-uc-71:-confirm-payment}

| Primary Actors | Cashier | Secondary Actors | PayOS (bank-transfer QR)  |
| ----: | :---- | ----: | :---- |
| **Description** | As a Cashier, I want to confirm that the patient has paid a receipt and record the payment method, so that the patient can continue: an examination fee puts the visit in the room's examination waiting list, and a paraclinical fee releases the orders of UC-49 and routes them to the least busy room that performs each service (BR-15, BR-26, BR-28). A visit whose examination fee has a patient amount pays it before the examination, and pays one paraclinical fee for each order before the paraclinical rooms. The software only records the "paid" confirmation (BR-36).  |  |  |
| **Preconditions** | 1\. The Cashier has selected a Pending receipt (UC-69 or UC-70). 2\. The patient is at the counter.  |  |  |
| **Normal Flow** | 1\. The system shows the receipt detail: receipt code, type, patient, registration code, visit type and coverage rate, and the lines: service, code, quantity, unit price, insurance amount, patient amount; totals (BR-27). Receipts never contain medication (BR-33). 2\. The Cashier tells the patient the amount to pay. 3\. The Cashier chooses Collect cash (Thu tiền mặt tại quầy), or shows the PayOS bank-transfer QR code (Thanh toán QR PayOS – BR-109). 4\. The system checks that the receipt is still Pending (the receipt is locked while it is confirmed – BR-118). 5\. For cash, the system shows MSG06 with the amount and an optional note; for PayOS, the system checks the payment every 3 seconds. 6\. The Cashier confirms (for PayOS: the payment is confirmed only when PayOS itself reports it paid). 7\. The system sets the receipt to Paid with the payment method, Cashier, paid time and receipt number (PT \+ date \+ receipt code – BR-53), and records it in the audit log (BR-37). 8\. The system continues the visit according to the receipt type: – Examination fee: the visit becomes Waiting and appears in the examination waiting list of its room (BR-15, BR-18); – Paraclinical fee: each order becomes Waiting and is routed to the Active room with the fewest waiting orders among the rooms that perform the service (ties: lower room code – BR-26, BR-28). 9\. The system shows MSG29 with the receipt number and the room of each paraclinical service, and opens the receipt print (UC-72).  |  |  |
| **Alternative Flows** | **AF-01 (at step 2): The patient does not agree to pay now** 1\. The Cashier closes the receipt without confirming; it stays Pending. If it is not paid by the end of the day, it is cancelled and the visit becomes Abandoned (BR-22). \=\> The use case ends. **AF-02 (at step 8): No Active room performs a service** 1\. The order stays Waiting without a room; the system warns the Cashier ("Chưa có phòng đang hoạt động cho …") and the audit entry lists the service. \=\> Continue at step 9\.  |  |  |
| **Exception Flows** | **EF-01 (at step 3): No payment method** 1\. The system shows MSG02. \=\> Return to step 3\. **EF-02 (at step 4): The receipt is no longer Pending (already paid or cancelled)** 1\. The system shows MSG60 and reloads the receipt list. \=\> The use case ends. **EF-03 (at step 7): Session expired or system error** 1\. The system shows MSG12 or MSG80; the receipt stays Pending (all or nothing). \=\> Return to step 3\.  |  |  |
| **Postconditions** | Success: the receipt is Paid and cannot be edited or deleted; the patient is in the room's examination waiting list (examination fee) or each order is in the waiting list of its paraclinical room (paraclinical fee). Failure / Cancelled: the receipt stays Pending.  |  |  |
| **Business Rules** | BR-15, BR-18, BR-22, BR-26, BR-27, BR-28, BR-33, BR-36, BR-37, BR-53, BR-109, BR-118; Data rule: Paid payments are permanent (I.3.3)  |  |  |
| **Messages** | MSG02, MSG06, MSG12, MSG29, MSG60, MSG80  |  |  |

### **13.4 UC-72: Print Payment Receipt** {#13.4-uc-72:-print-payment-receipt}

| Primary Actors | Cashier | Secondary Actors | None |
| ----: | :---- | ----: | :---- |
| **Description** | As a Cashier, I want to print the receipt for the patient after the payment is confirmed, so that the patient has proof of payment and, for paraclinical fees, knows the rooms to go to. Receipts can only be printed after payment is confirmed, or when the receipt is Exempt (BR-36, BR-37).  |  |  |
| **Preconditions** | 1\. The receipt is Paid (UC-71) or Exempt.  |  |  |
| **Normal Flow** | 1\. The Cashier clicks Print Receipt (In phiếu thu) on the receipt detail (the system also opens the print right after UC-71 on that screen). 2\. The system builds the receipt (PF-06): facility name, receipt number, patient name and code, registration code, visit type and coverage rate, room, lines with service, unit price, insurance amount and patient amount, totals, payment method, Cashier, paid time. 3\. For a paraclinical receipt, the system adds the assigned room of each service (BR-28), or "Chưa có phòng thực hiện" (UC-71 AF-02); for an examination fee receipt, the room and queue number of the visit. 4\. The system records the print in the audit log, shows a preview and opens the print dialog of the browser. 5\. The Cashier hands the receipt to the patient. |  |  |
| **Alternative Flows** | **AF-01 (at step 1): Reprint (from UC-70 or UC-73)** 1\. The Cashier opens a Paid receipt and clicks Print; from the second print the receipt is marked "BẢN SAO" and the reprint is logged. \=\> Continue at step 4\.  |  |  |
| **Exception Flows** | **EF-01 (at step 1): The receipt is not Paid or Exempt** 1\. The system shows MSG58 and does not print. \=\> The use case ends. **EF-02 (at step 4): The printer fails** 1\. TBD: the browser does not report printer errors, so MSG49 cannot be shown. The payment is not affected. \=\> The use case ends. **EF-03 (any step): Session expired or system error** 1\. The system shows MSG12 or MSG80. \=\> The use case ends.  |  |  |
| **Postconditions** | The patient receives the printed receipt. No business data is changed; each print is in the audit log.  |  |  |
| **Business Rules** | BR-27, BR-28, BR-33, BR-36, BR-37 |  |  |
| **Messages** | MSG12, MSG49, MSG58, MSG80  |  |  |

### **13.5 UC-73: View Payment History** {#13.5-uc-73:-view-payment-history}

| Primary Actors | Cashier | Secondary Actors | None |
| ----: | :---- | ----: | :---- |
| **Description** | As a Cashier, I want to view the history of receipts that have been paid or cancelled, so that I can check what I collected during my shift and answer patients' questions. Paid receipts cannot be changed (BR-37).  |  |  |
| **Preconditions** | 1\. The Cashier is signed in (UC-01). |  |  |
| **Normal Flow** | 1\. The Cashier selects Payment History (Lịch sử thanh toán). 2\. The system shows the filters: From date and To date (default: today), Status (Tất cả, Đã thanh toán, Đã hủy), Type (Phí khám, Cận lâm sàng), Payment method (Tiền mặt, Chuyển khoản, Thẻ), Cashier (Của tôi – default, Tất cả thu ngân), Sort (time newest/oldest, amount highest/lowest). 3\. The Cashier selects the filters and clicks View (Xem). 4\. The system shows the receipts whose paid or cancelled time is in the range: receipt number, type, status, patient, registration code, time, payment method, patient amount, insurance amount; plus the patient amount per payment method and the total over all matching Paid receipts. 5\. The Cashier selects a receipt. 6\. The system shows its detail (lines, amounts) and the Print action for Paid receipts (UC-72).  |  |  |
| **Alternative Flows** | **None** |  |  |
| **Exception Flows** | **EF-01 (at step 3): Start date after end date** 1\. The system shows MSG50 and does not search. \=\> Return to step 3\. **EF-02 (at step 4): No receipt matches** 1\. The system shows MSG01. \=\> Return to step 3\. **EF-03 (any step): Session expired or system error** 1\. The system shows MSG12 or MSG80. \=\> The use case ends.  |  |  |
| **Postconditions** | The payment history is shown. No data is changed. |  |  |
| **Business Rules** | BR-22, BR-36, BR-37, BR-111  |  |  |
| **Messages** | MSG01, MSG12, MSG50, MSG80  |  |  |

## **14\. System Administration**

### **14.1 UC-77: Update Clinic Facility Information** 

| Primary Actors | Cashier | Secondary Actors | None |
| ----: | :---- | ----: | :---- |
| **Description** | As an Admin, I want to declare and update the information of the clinic facility (facility code, name, address, phone, operating licence number, organization form), so that it is printed correctly on examination tickets, receipts and other documents. The facility code cannot change once a visit exists, because it is printed on examination documents (BR-48).  |  |  |
| **Preconditions** | 1\. The Admin is signed in and does not have to change the password first (UC-01, UC-03).  |  |  |
| **Normal Flow** | 1\. The Admin opens Hospital Information (Thông tin bệnh viện). 2\. The system shows the current information and its status (code locked or still changeable, last updated), or an empty form with the button "Khai báo cơ sở" when the facility has not been declared yet. 3\. The Admin edits the fields: Facility code (Mã cơ sở KBCB)\*, Facility name\*, Address\*, Phone\*, Operating licence number\*, Organization form\*. The facility code field is disabled when a visit exists. 4\. The Admin clicks Save (Lưu thay đổi). The button stays disabled until a field changes. 5\. The system checks the fields (BR-66): facility code exactly 5 digits; name at most 255 characters; address at most 1,024 characters; phone: mobile 0\[3\|5\|7\|8\|9\] \+ 8 digits, landline 02 \+ 9 digits, or 1800/1900 hotline; licence number at most 100 characters; organization form chosen from the list. Leading and trailing spaces are removed. The server repeats the check. 6\. The system checks that the information was not changed by another user since it was opened (BR-119) and that the facility code is not changed after the first visit (BR-48). 7\. The system saves the information and records the changed fields with old and new values in the audit log. 8\. The system shows MSG03 (or MSG04 for the first declaration) and the saved information.  |  |  |
| **Alternative Flows** | **AF-01 (at step 4): The address or the organization form was changed** 1\. The system reminds the Admin to check the operating licence number ("Kiểm tra giấy phép hoạt động"). 2\. The Admin clicks "Vẫn lưu" to continue, or "Quay lại sửa" to return to step 3\. \=\> Continue at step 5\. **AF-02 (at step 4): Nothing was changed** 1\. Save stays disabled; nothing is saved and no audit entry is written. \=\> The use case ends.  |  |  |
| **Exception Flows** | **EF-01 (at step 5): Required field empty, too long or wrong format** 1\. The system shows MSG02, MSG08 or MSG05 under the field. \=\> Return to step 3\. **EF-02 (at step 6): The facility code is changed after the first visit** 1\. The system shows MSG91, reloads the saved code and keeps the other edits. \=\> Return to step 3\. **EF-03 (at step 6): The information was changed by another user** 1\. The system shows MSG75 and reloads the latest information. \=\> Return to step 3\. **EF-04 (at step 1): The user is not an Admin** 1\. The system shows MSG13. \=\> The use case ends. **EF-05 (any step): Session expired or system error** 1\. The system shows MSG12 or MSG80. \=\> The use case ends.  |  |  |
| **Postconditions** | Success: the facility information is saved and used on documents printed afterwards; documents already printed are not changed. The change is in the audit log. Failure: nothing is changed.  |  |  |
| **Business Rules** | Success: the facility information is saved and used on documents printed afterwards; documents already printed are not changed. The change is in the audit log.  |  |  |
| **Messages** | MSG02, MSG03, MSG04, MSG05, MSG08, MSG12, MSG13, MSG75, MSG80, MSG91  |  |  |

## **15\.  Shift schedule management**

### **15.1 UC-95 View Duty Schedule List** 

| Primary Actors | Admin | Secondary Actors | None |
| ----: | :---- | ----: | :---- |
| **Description** | Allows the Administrator to search, track, and display the weekly duty schedule matrix for medical staff (Doctors, Technicians) assigned to each clinic room by work shifts (Morning Shift / Afternoon Shift). |  |  |
| **Preconditions** | 1\. The user has successfully logged into the system with the ADMIN role. 2\. Department, Room, and Staff Account catalog data already exist in the system. |  |  |
| **Normal Flow** | 1\. Admin navigates to the "Duty Schedule" menu on the navigation bar. 2\. The system retrieves the current date (according to the Asia/Ho\_Chi\_Minh timezone), determines the current week (Monday to Sunday), and sends a request to fetch the duty shift configuration data and this week's assignment matrix. 3\. The system displays the weekly duty schedule matrix interface: • Page title, displayed week (from date \- to date). • Shift filter: \[All shifts\], \[Morning Shift (configured time)\], \[Afternoon Shift (configured time)\]. • Matrix table: Columns are days of the week (Monday → Sunday with specific dates, current date is highlighted); Rows are grouped by Department and detailed Clinic Room. • Each schedule cell displays the responsible staff information (Full name, title: Doctor / Technician) or \[Unassigned\] status. 4\. Admin can use the week navigation buttons (\< Previous Week, \> Next Week, This Week) to view schedules for different weeks. 5\. Admin can click to switch between shift filter tabs: All Shifts, Morning Shift, Afternoon Shift to accurately display the required shift. |  |  |
| **Alternative Flows** | **AF-01: Filter by specific work shift** 1\. At step 3 of Normal Flow, Admin selects the Morning Shift or Afternoon Shift tab. *2\. The matrix table filters and displays only duty shifts matching the selected shift.* **AF-02: Switch viewed week** 1\. Admin clicks the \< (Previous Week) or \> (Next Week) icon, or the This Week button. *2\. The system reloads the duty schedule data corresponding to the selected week's time range and updates the display.* |  |  |
| **Exception Flows** | **EF-01: Network disconnection or server error (API Error)** 1\. When weekly schedule loading fails, the system stops loading and displays an error message. *2\. Displays a "Retry" button for Admin to resend the data loading request.* **EF-02: Expired login session or insufficient privileges** 1\. The system detects an expired/invalid token. *2\. Redirects the user to the Login page with a notification that the working session has ended.* |  |  |
| **Postconditions** | Admin grasps all information regarding personnel arrangements on duty at clinic rooms for the selected week. |  |  |
| **Business Rules** | BR1, BR2, BR3, BR4 |  |  |
| **Messages** | Loading duty schedule..., Cannot load duty schedule. Please try again., Unassigned |  |  |

| ----: | :---- | ----: | :---- |

The system displays an error if attempting to assign a Technician to a Clinical examination room or a Doctor to a Paraclinical room without valid role permissions. |  |  |
